analysis:
Examined both added changelogs, file modes, the inference-documentation patch and all supplied BASE surroundings against the canonical definition index and detailed T-041 evidence. These units contain documentation, not executable controls; no independently supported security regression was identified.
changelog.d/glm-openrouter-returned-reasoning.md:3-7 describes accepting strict tools with post-generation schema validation, incorporating consumer-supplied historical reasoning, normalizing empty arguments and widening thinking-control syntax. Integration must verify GLM5NextPromptPolicy and ToolConstraintValidation actually withhold invalid calls before any streaming exposure, retain conflicting/hidden-reasoning refusals, and keep rendered-history changes bound to the appropriate prompt/cache identity (A-001, T-007, T-041, TB-007). Full reasoning rather than requested summaries is explicitly documented; this alone does not establish cross-user disclosure.
changelog.d/glm-variable-frame-rate-video.md:3 and docs/architecture/inference.md HEAD patch lines 810-815 describe admitting variable-rate tracks using presentation-order indices and nominalFrameRate, while retaining sampling and decoded-byte limits. Integration should examine GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset and GLM5NextVisionBudget to establish finite rate handling, bounds on actual decode work and allocations, cancellation, and plaintext-media custody (T-010, T-050, TB-007). The patch also states media remain excluded from prefix reuse; implementation is not supplied here.
BASE inference.md:643-801 describes existing artifact pinning, native ownership, memory admission and managed-serving restrictions; none is changed in these units. No changes to authorization, attestation, hop encryption, billing or privileged-helper authority are evidenced. Remaining uncertainty concerns implementation of the newly documented request and media acceptance paths, to be reconciled in the source/integration passes rather than treated as a proven missing control.
